title: Guidelines for Registration of Biological Products 2025
text:
Review Date: 09-04-2025 Doc. Ref. No. VBM-R&RA-GDL-012-00
Effective Date: 08-04-2030
National Agency for Food & Drug Administration & Control
(NAFDAC)
Vaccine, Biologics and Medical Devices Registration
& Regulatory Affairs (VBM-R&RA) Directorate
GUIDELINES FOR REGISTRATION BIOLOGICAL
PRODUCTS
Page 1 of 10

Review Date: 09-04-2025 Doc. Ref. No. VBM-R&RA-GDL-012-00
Effective Date: 08-04-2030
1.0. General
1.1. These Guidelines are for the interest of the general public and, in particular,
importers of biological products for human and veterinary use in Nigeria.
1.2. It is necessary to emphasize that no drug shall be manufactured, imported,
exported, advertised, sold, distributed, or used in Nigeria unless it has been
registered in accordance with the provisions of NAFDAC Act CAP N1 (LFN) 2004,
other related Legislations, and the accompanying Guidelines.
1.3. NAFDAC will not entertain new applications for the registration of imported
regulated products on the Federal Government Import Prohibition List, NAFDAC
Ceiling List, and banned formulations.
2.0. Dossier Submission and Validation
2.1 To initiate the registration process for a biological product, the applicant is required
to submit the Dossier of the product for screening.
2.2 The dossier should be prepared in accordance with the format outlined in the
relevant NAFDAC guideline for preparation of technical information related to the
intended biological product (Veterinary vaccine, Human vaccine, Biosimilar,
Biotherapeutic products) for registration.
2.3 Each module of the dossier should be placed in a separate folder and properly
labelled with the applicant's name and the product name as a suffix (e.g., XYZ
Limited—Rituximab 200mg Injection-Module 1).
2.4 Each file in the dossier should be in searchable PDF format, except for the QOS
and QIS, which should be in Word document format.
2.5 Applicants should send an email to vb.vbmrr@nafdac.gov.ng, requesting access
to submit their product dossier(s) and specifying the number of dossiers to be
submitted.
2.6 In response to the email, a unique link for uploading the dossiers will be provided
to the applicant. (For video description of the upload process, please click on this
Link)
2.7 Upon successful completion of the screening process, applicants will be issued a
Dossier Screening Clearance.
2.8 Dossier Screening clearance is a prerequisite for submission of applications for
registration of biological products on the NAFDAC Automated Products Administration
and Monitoring System (NAPAMS) platform.

3.0. Applications
3.1 The Application for the registration of all biological products should be processed on
the NAPAMS portal - https://registration.nafdac.gov.ng. For more information, see
the NAPAMS User Manual.
3.2 A separate application form shall be submitted for each product.
Step 1
4.0. Documentation
The following documents should be uploaded on the NAPAMS portal. After successful
submission, all original documents will be presented upon request.
4.1. Dossier Screening Clearance
4.2. An application letter addressed to the Director-General (NAFDAC), Attention: Director,
Vaccine, Biologics and Medical Devices Registration & Regulatory Affairs Directorate,
NAFDAC Office Complex, Apapa-Oshodi Expressway, Isolo, Lagos State.
4.3. A Notarized Declaration (Appendix I) to be completed (typed) and signed by the
Declarant and notarized by a Notary Public in Nigeria.
4.4. A Power of Attorney (where the applicant does not own the product brand name) or
Contract Manufacturing Agreement (where the applicant owns the Brand name).
4.5. The Power of Attorney shall be:
4.5.1 Issued by the manufacturer of the product.
4.5.2 Signed by the Managing Director, General Manager, Chairman or President of
the Company, stating the names of the products to be registered. The Power
of Attorney shall also state ‘Authority to register product with NAFDAC’.
4.5.3 State ownership of Brand name(s)/Trademark.
4.5.4 Notarized by a Notary Public in the Country of manufacture.
4.5.5 Valid for at least five (5) years.
4.6. The Contract Manufacturing Agreement shall be:
4.6.1 Notarized by a Notary Public in the country of manufacture.
4.6.2 Signed by both parties, stating names and designations of the signatories, with
the names of all the products to be registered and other relevant clauses clearly
explained in an unambiguous language.
4.7. Evidence of Business Incorporation of the applicant with the Corporate Affairs
Commission in Nigeria.
4.8. Manufacturing License/Certificate of Free Sale - Evidence that the manufacturer is
licensed to manufacture drugs for sale in the country of origin (Manufacturer’s
Certificate). The license shall be issued by a relevant Health/Regulatory body in the
country of manufacture.

Effective Date: 08-04-2030
4.9. Certificate of Pharmaceutical Product (COPP-WHO Format). There must be evidence
certification by the competent Health Authority that the sale of the product does not
constitute a contravention of the drug laws of that country. The Certificate of
Pharmaceutical Product (COPP) should;
4.9.1 Conform to the WHO format.
4.9.2 Be issued by the Health/Regulatory body in the country of manufacture.
4.9.3 The COPP must be authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission
in the country of origin. However, any Commonwealth or ECOWAS country can
authenticate the COPP in countries without a Nigerian Embassy.
4.10. Current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) certificate of the manufacturing facility,
which should be:
4.10.1 Valid at the time of submission.
4.10.2 Issued by the Health/Regulatory body in the country of manufacture.
4.10.3 Be authenticated by the Nigerian Embassy or High Commission in the country
of origin. In countries where no Nigerian Embassy exists, any
Commonwealth or ECOWAS country can authenticate the document.
4.11. Evidence of Registration of Brand Name with Trademark Registry in the Ministry of
Industry, Trade and Investment. This should be registered in the name of the owner
of the Trademark/Brand name, as the case may be (registration of Trademark should
be in Class 5).
4.12. Product Labels/artwork which should comply with the following requirements:
4.12.1 Labelling should be informative and accurate.
4.12.2 Name of the product (brand name), where applicable, and generic name.
4.12.3 Where a brand name is used, there MUST be the generic name, which should
be conspicuous, written directly under the brand name.
4.12.4 Name and full location address of the manufacturer.
4.12.5 Provision for NAFDAC Registration Number on product label
4.12.6 Batch No., Manufacturing date, and Expiry date.
4.12.7 Dosage form & strength
4.12.8 Indications, frequency, route, conditions of administration (Over the
counter; OTC drugs).
4.12.9 Dosage regimen on the package (Over the Counter; OTC drugs).
4.12.10 Patient Information Leaflet (PIL)
4.12.11 Prescribing information (for POM).
4.12.12 Net content of product
4.12.13 Quantitative listing of all the active ingredients per unit dose
4.12.14 Adequate warnings (where applicable).
4.12.15 Storage conditions
4.12.16 Withdrawal Period for Veterinary Vaccines (where applicable)
Note: Any drug product whose name or package label bears a close resemblance to

an already registered product or is likely to be mistaken for such registered product
shall not be considered for registration.
Any Biological product labelled in a foreign language shall NOT be considered for
registration unless an English translation is included on the label and PIL (where
applicable).
See the Agency’s Drug Labelling Regulations and other relevant Regulations for
specific details.
4.13. A copy of a valid annual license to practice as the superintendent pharmacist issued
by the Pharmacy Council of Nigeria (PCN) (for human or veterinary products).
4.14. Evidence of a valid Certificate of Retention of Premises Registration for the facility.
4.15. Letter of Invitation for Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) Inspection: A letter of
invitation to inspect the factory abroad should be written by the manufacturer and
should state the following:
4.14.1 Manufacturer Information: The name of the company, the full location
address of the factory (not the administrative office address), the e-mail and
current phone number, and the details (name, phone number, and email) of
the contact person overseas.
4.14.2 Local Agent Information: The name of the company, full location address,
functional phone number, e-mail address, and details (name, phone number,
and email) of the contact person. Name(s) of product(s) for registration.
Note: Upon successfully applying for product registration on the NAPAMS platform, an
applicant is required to notify the Directorate of the submission via email at
vb.vbmrr@nafdac.gov.ng, stating the application number(s). This notification is
necessary to facilitate the progression of the product dossier to full review.
Step II
5.0. Issuance of Import Permit (for imported biological products)
5.1. Upon satisfactory review of submitted documents and label, a Permit to
Import will be issued electronically via the NAPAMS Portal to the applicant to
import registration samples for laboratory testing.
STEP III
6.0. Submission of laboratory samples
6.1. To ensure that laboratory samples are maintained under the recommended storage
conditions, applicants are required to submit the samples directly to the Laboratory.
Upon provision of the following documents, the applicant will be issued a letter
authorizing this direct submission:
6.1.1 An application requesting authorization to submit samples of a biological
Page 5 of 10

Review Date: 09-04-2025 Doc. Ref. No. VBM-R&RA-GDL-012-00
Effective Date: 08-04-2030
product directly to the laboratory for analysis. The application should include
the following information:
a. Physical description of the product
b. Batch number
c. Date of manufacture
d. Expiry date
Note: Items (b), (c), and (d) above must match the details stated on the label of
the product being submitted to the Laboratory.
6.1.2. Evidence of payment of processing fee.
6.1.3. A copy of the Permit to Import registration samples.
6.2. When submitting the samples to the laboratory, the Letter of Authorization should be
accompanied by the following documents:
6.2.1. Product dossier in a compact disc.
6.2.2. Certificate of analysis.
The Certificate of Analysis must be presented on the letterhead of the quality control
laboratory where the sample was tested or evaluated. It should include the outcomes
of the tested parameters, along with the following details:
a. The brand name of the product
b. The batch number of the product
c. The manufacturing and expiry dates
d. The name, designation, and signature of the analyst
Note: Items (b) and (c) above must match the details stated on the label of the
product being submitted to the Laboratory.
6.2.3. Vaccine Arrival Report
Step IV
7.0. Inspection of Local Cold Chain Storage and Manufacturing Facilities
7.1. For further information regarding the inspection of local cold chain storage and
manufacturing facilities, applicants are advised to contact the relevant directorates
of the Agency as follows:
7.1.1 Drug Evaluation and Research (DER) Directorate at
der.headquarters@nafdac.gov.ng for inquiries related to human vaccines
and biologics.
7.1.2 Veterinary Medicines and Allied Products (VMAP) Directorate at
vmap@nafdac.gov.ng for inquiries related to veterinary vaccines.
Step V

8.0. Product Approval meeting
8.1. Upon satisfactory technical documents review, GMP inspection of the production
facility, cold chain storage facility, and laboratory analysis of product (where
applicable), the product will be presented for consideration at the Food and Drug
Registration Committee (FDRC) Approval Meetings.
Step VI
8.0. Issuance of Certificate of Product Registration
8.1. For products approved at the FDRC meeting, an electronic Certificate of
Product Registration will be issued to the applicant on the NAPAMS portal.
10.0. Tariff
10.1. Please refer to the relevant section of the NAFDAC Tariff.
11.0. Note:
11.1. For all biological products, including New Biological Entities (NBE), there must be
evidence that Clinical Trials have been undertaken in an acceptable population.
11.2. If the materials used in the product formulation are derived from blood, the
following information must be provided in the appropriate module of the dossier:
11.2.1 A Plasma Master File containing details of the plasma source, including
collection methods, the complete production process, in-process controls,
and viral safety measures.
11.2.2 A Notarized certificate confirming the plasma is free from HIV-1, HIV-2,
HBsAg, and HCV.
11.2.3 A copy of the certificate of release from the health authority (applicable to
drug substances only).
11.3. Failure to comply with these requirements may result in the rejection of the
application.
11.4. A successful application will be issued with a Certificate of Registration with a
validity period of five (5) years.
11.5. Registration of a product does not automatically confer an Advertising Permit. A
separate application and subsequent approval by the Agency shall be required if
the product is to be advertised. For further information on advert approvals, see
the NAFDAC Guidelines for Advertisement of Medical Products, Cosmetics,
Veterinary products and finished Chemicals.
11.6. NAFDAC reserves the right to revoke, suspend, or vary a certificate during its
Page 7 of 10

validity period.
11.7. Failure to respond promptly to queries or enquiries raised by NAFDAC on the
application (within 60 workdays) will automatically result in the archival of the
application on NAPAMS.
11.8. The timeline for product registration from acceptance of submissions to issuance of
the product certificate of Registration is two hundred and forty (240)
workdays.
11.9. Please note that the clock stops once compliances are issued.
